verdict.rationale: Aider's core interaction is natural-language instruction: users type requests in chat, pass one-shot instructions via `--message` or `coder.run()`, and ask questions in `/ask` mode. They can also speak instructions via `/voice` or leave `AI!`/`AI?` comments in watch mode, and Aider can infer which files to edit from the request. Community users corroborate the chat workflow, including natural-language questions and editor comments like '# make this darker ai!'. Missing for 10: session and file management (adding files, undo, git operations, model switching) still relies on explicit slash commands rather than plain natural language.
